title: LabBuilder: Protocol-Grounded 3D Layout Generation for Interactable and Safe Laboratory
claim: A multi-part system combines knowledge bases and constraint-aware generation to produce valid, safe layouts, outperforming prior methods on key metrics.
layout: Top 3D scene with side insets; bottom row of knowledge bases and charts
description: A wide figure in two bands. The top band is a pink-tinted panel with a large rendered 3D laboratory in the center: benchtops, a fume hood, instruments and a blue floor. Red dashed circles and diagonal text mark problems such as 'flammable reagent close to heat source', 'collision' and 'navigation initialize/add'. On the left, two top-down floor plans with robot-view circles show navigation failure (red dashed, 'endpoint invalidity') refined into success (green dashed). On the right, circled before/after views show fixes by FastRepair and LLMAdjust, labelled geometry validity and chemical safety, with green shield checkmarks. The bottom band has three parts: an Asset Knowledge Base (geometry and semantic cards, property checklists, Heating plate and Ethyl Acetate cards), a Chemical Knowledge Base (reaction schemes with reagents), and a bar chart and line plot comparing SceneWeaver, Holodeck and LabBuilder on chemical safety and geometric violations.
caption: Overview of LabBuilder. We construct both an asset knowledge base and a chemical knowledge base from heterogeneous inputs, and synthesize asset-grounded experimental protocols. Based on these protocols, we generate laboratory layouts that ensure navigational feasibility, geometric validity, and chemical safety. LabBuilder achieves the best performance compared to existing methods.
abstract: Automated laboratories hold the promise of accelerating scientific discovery, yet their deployment is bottlenecked by the difficulty of designing safe and executable environments. While simulator-based design offers scalability, existing 3D scene generation methods are primarily tailored for household settings, optimizing for visual plausibility while neglecting the protocol grounding and layout-level safety constraints essential for scientific experimentation. We present LabBuilder, an end-to-end system that generates and verifies 3D laboratory layouts from concise textual specifications. It operates through three tightly coupled components: LabForge first curates a meta-dataset of annotated assets and chemical knowledge, translating natural language specifications into structured protocols; building on these protocols, LabGen synthesizes laboratory layouts via an iterative, constraint-aware optimization strategy; finally, LabTouchstone evaluates the resulting layouts as a unified benchmark. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LabBuilder significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, producing laboratory environments that are realistic and valid under modeled geometric, chemical-safety, and navigation constraints.
